name: Dark Violet-Slate
lede: Dark Violet-Slate is a dark, cool grey with only a faint purple cast, Robert Ridgway's darker step down from his own Violet-Slate.

sections.title: A grey with a whisper of violet
sections.body: Ridgway recorded Dark Violet-Slate in 1912, at plate XLIX, hue 53 quadruple-prime, tone k, directly below [[blue-slate|Violet-Slate]] on the same card [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary filed this darker name again in 1955, block 186, as a plain grayish blue, which is how little of the violet survives at this depth [2]. Measured in LCH, the hue sits at only chroma 7, so the color reads first as grey and only faintly as violet [1]. Its nearest named neighbors on file are [[dark-violet-grey]] and [[dark-payne-s-grey]], both almost the same at 3.1 to 3.3 CIEDE2000 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey, as photographed, in 501 of 23,781 paintings, 2.11 percent, more common than 70 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, 42 of 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.6 times the expected rate [4]. Gustav Klimt is its most devoted painter here, in 4 of his 50 works, 4.1 times the baseline rate [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow across its 194 strongest matches, and it is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.4 times the expected rate [4].
